audits.mathematicalReason: The large circle has diameter a+b. A semicircle of diameter d has area πd²/8, so the shaded area is S=π((a+b)²+a²−b²)/8=πa(a+b)/4. The unshaded area is U=π((a+b)²−a²+b²)/8=πb(a+b)/4. Since a,b>0, S/U=a/b. Composite-area reasoning and circle areas are assessed; expansion, factoring and cancellation appropriately support this method.

audits.mathematicalReason: On the scale increasing from the left baseline, BA reads approximately 20° and BD approximately 160°. Since ∠CBD=90°, BC reads approximately 160°−90°=70°. Thus ∠ABC≈70°−20°=50°. Reading a common protractor scale and subtracting angles directly match the candidate scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: The displayed pattern subdivides the nth triangle into n² equal-area triangular cells and shades the downward-pointing cells, numbering 1+2+⋯+(n−1)=n(n−1)/2. Equal bases and heights justify equal cell areas using the triangle-area formula, although numerical areas need not be calculated. For n=8, the shaded fraction is 28/64=7/16. Pattern generalization and interpreting a fraction of the whole are appropriate assessed scopes.

figureEvidence.fact: The four displayed triangles have respectively 0, 1, 3 and 6 shaded downward-pointing triangular cells.
The successive subdivisions have 1, 2, 3 and 4 equal intervals along each outer side, giving equal-area triangular grids with 1, 4, 9 and 16 cells.

audits.mathematicalReason: Take A=(−1,0) and B=(1,0). The given 120° angles and side lengths place E=(−2,√3) and C=(2,√3). Hence EC=4 and trapezoid EABC has area (4+2)√3/2=3√3. Since CD=DE=EC=4, triangle CDE is equilateral with area 4√3; convexity selects D on the opposite side of EC from AB. The total is 7√3. The alternative route is also valid: extending EA and CB below AB to meet at F makes FAB equilateral of side 2, while FE=FC=DE=DC=4 makes EDCF a rhombus. Its area is 8√3, and subtracting [FAB]=√3 gives the same result. These are alternative routes, not jointly required methods.

audits.mathematicalReason: At exactly 10 o'clock, the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand to 10. Each hour interval subtends 360°/12=30°, and the smaller separation spans two intervals. Thus the smaller angle is 2×30°=60°. This directly assesses angle calculation.

figureEvidence.fact: The clock face has twelve equally spaced hour positions around its center; the short route from 10 to 12 passes through 11.
No hands are drawn, so their positions are supplied by the stated time rather than read from the image.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let A and d denote the degree measures of ∠BAC and ∠BDC. The intercepted minor arc BC has central angle 2A by the inscribed-angle theorem. Radii to B and C are perpendicular to the tangents, so the angle sum in quadrilateral OBDC gives 2A+d=180°. The triangle angle sum and the given base angles give A+4d=180°. Solving yields A=540/7 degrees and d=180/7 degrees, hence x=(540/7)(π/180)=3π/7. The base angles are 360/7 degrees, so all three triangle angles are acute, consistent with the stated branch.

figureEvidence.fact: A, B and C lie on the circle; the tangent segments from B and C meet at the exterior point D.
A lies on the arc BC opposite D, and x labels the interior angle BAC. The relevant tangent angle is the interior angle BDC.

audits.mathematicalReason: The overlap is a parallelogram with horizontal altitude 1. Let its horizontal base length be L and let θ=π−α be the acute angle between the strip directions. The perpendicular width of the oblique strip gives L sin θ=1. Since sin(π−α)=sin α, its area is L×1=1/sin α. For the depicted nonparallel strips, 0<α<π and sin α>0. The acute-angle sine definition and supplementary-angle identity appropriately support the parallelogram-area calculation.

figureEvidence.fact: Each strip is bounded by a pair of parallel lines, and each perpendicular width is labelled 1.
The shaded overlap is a parallelogram; α is the obtuse interior angle between a horizontal side and an oblique side.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each triangle has side 2√3 and height √((2√3)²−(√3)²)=3, so its area is 3√3. Consecutive triangles are translated along the baseline by half a side. Each adjacent overlap is therefore an equilateral triangle with side ratio 1/2 and area one quarter of a full triangle. There are four positive-area overlaps; nonadjacent triangles have no positive-area intersection. Thus the union area is 5(3√3)−4(3√3/4)=12√3. Composite-area subtraction is assessed, and the listed triangle and similarity facts support this valid method.

figureEvidence.fact: Five equally sized, upward-pointing equilateral triangles share one baseline and are successively shifted to the right by half a base length.
There are four adjacent triangular overlap regions. Triangles separated by one intervening triangle meet only at a baseline vertex, so higher intersections contribute zero area.
